text: I'll start with the paged deployment and its pending pod.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks for 512 whole CPU cores per pod. Its pod template sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512", which Kubernetes reads as 512 cores, not the 512 millicores ("512m") that was clearly intended. The only node in the cluster, incident-lab-control-plane, has 6 allocatable CPUs, so no node can satisfy the request and the scheduler rejects the pod with FailedScheduling / "Insufficient cpu". The pod fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh therefore stays Pending with PodScheduled=False and never runs, so the Deployment reports 0/1 ready and no fraud scores are produced. Fixing the unit on the CPU request in the Deployment's pod template (512m) makes the pod fit on the existing node.
arguments.mechanism: The Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512" — 512 whole cores — where "512m" (512 millicores) was intended, and the cluster's single node offers only 6 allocatable CPUs. The scheduler cannot fit the pod on any node, so the Deployment's replica is rejected at scheduling with "Insufficient cpu", stays Pending with PodScheduled=False, and the Deployment remains at 0/1 ready.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is Pending and unscheduled.
The pod was never assigned a node; scheduling failed for lack of CPU.
evidence.quote: Warning  FailedScheduling  1s    default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.

evidence.claim: The pod requests 512 CPU (cores), as rendered from the Deployment template.
The Deployment pod template is the object carrying the wrong-unit CPU request.
The only node in the cluster has 6 allocatable CPUs, far less than the 512 cores requested.

ruled_out.alternative: The pod is blocked by a node taint or an unschedulable/unhealthy node.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node is Ready and the scheduler's rejection reason is CPU, not taints; the pod also carries only the default not-ready/unreachable tolerations.

ruled_out.alternative: A nodeSelector or affinity in the pod template excludes the node.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod has no node selector at all, so no placement constraint other than resources applies.

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota or LimitRange in the fraud namespace is injecting or blocking the request.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace contains no ResourceQuota or LimitRange objects — only a ConfigMap and a ServiceAccount besides the workload.

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or a crashing container is keeping the workload at 0/1.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never reached a node, so no image pull or container start was ever attempted; its only condition is PodScheduled=False.
